findings.title: Rendering a small DOCX table can exhaust host memory
findings.summary:
An untrusted DOCX author can set huge positive w:gridSpan, w:gridBefore or w:gridAfter counts in a small, shallow table. Rendering sums those counts into grid occupancy and directly sizes column, preference and merge vectors. Counts of 1000000000/1073741824 request about 4 GB/4 GiB for f32 columns; 4294967295 requests approximately 16 GiB before additional allocations, despite package admission. Assigned discovery-0031 corroborates the existing one-billion-column, 4,000,000,000-byte f32-vector framing through both span and row-skip inputs; these are static counts.
 Assigned discovery-0032 corroborates the live span and both synthetic row-skip paths, including merge-slot expansion; separate Markdown span clamping does not protect rendering.
findings.remediation:
Enforce practical per-span and total-column budgets for gridSpan, gridBefore and gridAfter before excessive RawCell, column, preference or merge allocation/work. Use checked occupancy sums and col+span arithmetic, apply the same budget to every derived table vector, and return a typed resource-limit refusal on excess. Propagate a caller-adjustable semantic column limit through all public rendering surfaces and charge later column/merge vectors to that same budget.
Additional retained remediation detail: Enforce explicit maximum live cell spans, row skips, aggregate table columns and merge slots before any allocation. Use checked sums and a cumulative layout resource budget, returning a typed refusal when exceeded.

findings.title: Reading or converting nested legacy DOC fields can monopolize the processing thread
findings.summary: An attacker-authored Word 97–2003 DOC can repeatedly begin fields and enter their result sections, leaving an increasingly long all-false field stack. Story::blocks scans the entire stack before every input character, giving quadratic CPU work during reading/conversion and even the native Word-input refusal hint. Assigned discovery-0031 supplies a balanced result-state framing with approximately 100000 nested fields in a few hundred kilobytes, implying billions of boolean inspections. This is heap-stack scanning CPU cost, not recursive call-stack overflow.
findings.remediation: Maintain an O(1) active-code-frame count, updating it correctly on begin, separator and end while preserving suppression under any code ancestor. Enforce explicit field-nesting and processing-work budgets for balanced and malformed legacy field streams before excessive work. Keep legacy diagnostic probes cheap and bounded, or enforce the same field/work budgets before invoking the full reader solely for a refusal hint.

findings.title: Untrusted Markdown reference documents reach unchecked recursive XML parsing
findings.summary: Markdown conversion opens a caller-supplied reference DOCX using byte-only package bounds and parses its main XML without the XML-depth admission gate. A deeply nested reference can terminate the host processing it. The reference main part reaches section extraction irrespective of whether its body text is retained; Rust/Python/WASM and CLI reference paths share the boundary. Earlier low and assigned medium severity assessments are retained with their explicit untrusted-template prerequisite.
findings.remediation: Admit every supplied reference DOCX under explicit active InputLimits before metadata, style, scholar, frame or other reference XML consumers parse it, or consistently use checked parsing at every main and preserved auxiliary XML boundary. Propagate limits and typed refusals across Rust/Python/WASM/CLI paths.

findings.title: A shared font-index directory permits staging symlink overwrites
findings.summary: Native font-index saving writes to a predictable PID-based temporary file with fs::write. If an operator places the index in a directory writable by a less-trusted local user, that user can redirect a cache save to another victim-writable file.
findings.remediation: Publish the font index through an unpredictable private staging directory and an exclusively created regular file held open through writing. Atomically rename only that file; refuse preexisting staging entries and document/private-parent expectations for shared configurations.

findings.title: Python CLI output/plan and npm direct-output symlinks can overwrite unrelated files
findings.summary:
Python and npm ordinary-output helpers check pathname existence separately from truncating writes; a local writer of the selected directory can replace an output name and redirect generated bytes to a victim-writable file. Python plan recording additionally uses a predictable basename/PID partial pathname without exclusive creation. The assigned report also corroborates npm plan staging, which is represented by the separately retained symlink-following.plan-staging finding. Without --force, a stable symlink to an existing referent is refused; post-preflight substitution bypasses that refusal, and a dangling link can pass the existence test. Filesystem/OS protections and shared-directory authority remain prerequisites. The shared writers also publish read/compare/revision results, document/PDF/PNG and font/render products, edit/visual-diff bundles, field-update reports, and repair outputs. Assigned Python and npm diff/bundle traces explicitly include dangling destination links permitting unintended file creation without --force, and forced existing-member links redirecting bundle/report writes; stable existing referents are refused in the ordinary nonracing no-force case.
 Assigned discovery-0032 corroborates Python PDF/PNG publication and Node renderTo, with conversion between existence preflight and final write; shared mutable directory entries and distinct attacker/victim authority remain essential.
findings.remediation:
Publish Python/Node ordinary outputs, bundles and reports through held-directory authority and exclusive private staging. Atomically install without replacement when --force is false, or atomically replace the authorized destination entry when true; never truncate through a mutable final pathname. Apply exclusive unpredictable regular-file staging beside the authorized target to Python plan recording. Node recordPlan staging retains its separately established repair and identity. Expose/reuse native publication for Python CLI outputs with overwrite authorization passed into the commit operation; Node host publication must provide equivalent exclusive staging and atomic no-clobber/replacement. Preserve the documented final-output rule: forced publication replaces the selected symlink directory entry itself and leaves its referent unchanged; no-force installation must refuse an already occupied destination, including a dangling symlink.
Additional retained remediation detail: Use staged verified publication with held parent-directory authority for both wrappers. Carry overwrite authorization through commit and atomically refuse any existing destination when force is false; do not rely on a preliminary exists check.

findings.title: Cyclic Markdown drawing dependencies terminate conversion through unbounded recursion
findings.summary: A drawing: image destination in ordinary Markdown is base64-decoded and deserialized into a dependency graph without validation. Package materialization recursively follows each dep.rels.part before writing the dependent part and has no active-node or completed-node map. A one-node self-reference causes indefinite recursion and stack exhaustion, even with default Markdown conversion options and no image loader. Header/footer drawing payloads also reach this same materializer through view_stories::story_part. Capture memoizes a part before descending, so even capture-produced envelopes can encode a cycle; capture count/byte limits do not establish an acyclic imported graph. The supplied discovery-0030 trace additionally records that an empty boxes collection bypasses text-box-specific Writer finish checks; these checks do not validate the dependency graph.
findings.remediation: Validate dependency indices, count/byte/depth limits and graph shape at import. Materialize with an active/completed traversal state and index-to-output map, rejecting cycles or reserving identities to support cycles without recursive expansion. Memoize shared subgraphs. Enforce explicit dependency-edge and traversal-work budgets before assembly; when rejecting active-node revisits return a typed conversion refusal. Apply the same graph validation and traversal state to header/footer drawing materialization, not only body drawings.

findings.title: Tiny Markdown table metadata can trigger unbounded cell allocation
findings.summary: A caller-controlled cells paragraph range is converted into an unbounded count and used to append padding cells. A tiny Markdown table with a range such as p0-p1000000000 causes roughly a billion padding entries to be allocated before DOCX assembly, exhausting CPU and memory in Rust, Python, or WASM conversion hosts. The new corroboration explicitly matches two metadata ranges to a header and data row without breaks; MOST_GRID=64 and arithmetic overflow checks do not bound these valid row counts.
findings.remediation: Validate row_paragraphs with the same bounded range helper used elsewhere, impose a total table/output cell budget before allocation, and return a structured refusal rather than silently processing an oversized range.

findings.title: Unbounded list levels cause billions of iterations or allocations
findings.summary:
Paragraph and numbering-definition ilvl attributes accept arbitrary u32 values. Resolving an undefined high level scans every lower integer; defining the high level instead drives counter initialization and label substitution loops over the same enormous range. Abstract definitions and full lvlOverride records accept the same unchecked level IDs; both missing-level reverse search and defined-level counter/label work require bounded handling.
 Assigned discovery-0032 preserves the valid numbering-instance prerequisite and the distinct billion-level defined-counter variant as well as undefined-level backwards search.
findings.remediation:
Validate the supported ilvl domain in paragraph, style, abstract and override sources before use. Find fallback levels among actual defined keys and initialize/substitute only supported or defined levels; avoid any iteration or allocation proportional to an untrusted numeric level. Return a typed refusal for unsupported level metadata rather than attempting dense counter or placeholder materialization.
Additional retained remediation detail: Validate paragraph and numbering-definition level IDs against the supported 0..=8 range. Resolve ancestors by actual defined keys and bound synthesized counters and marker iteration independently of untrusted integer values.

findings.title: Entity decoding repeatedly scans the input suffix
findings.summary: HTML altChunk text with bare ampersands and the public XML entity decoder repeatedly search the remaining suffix for ';', yielding quadratic CPU work. A valid admitted .rels Target containing repeated & is normalized upstream and redundantly decoded by PartFs, reaching the same XML sink during rendering, inspection, revision processing or comparison even when the target part does not exist. An additional admitted-main-XML route uses an unquoted value whose first character never reappears: the DOM consumes through EOF and decodes a bare-ampersand comment as an attribute, reaching the same quadratic XML decoder. Ordinary bare-ampersand text is rejected upstream and is not this proof. The same HTML decoder is also reached by Markdown-to-DOCX raw HTML blocks and attribute values; its ten-byte accepted-entity bound is applied after the unbounded search. Assigned discovery-0031 corroborates both established decoders independently: ordinary HTML/MHT paragraph text reaches the HTML helper even when script/style content is skipped, while an internal fontTable target reaches redundant XML decoding before any absent-part lookup. Its supplied offline dependency evidence identifies oxml-opc 0.14.2 and quick-xml 0.41.0 attribute normalization, independently supported by the repository target round-trip test. No reducer dependency inspection occurred.
findings.remediation: Scan entities once without revisiting suffixes. In HTML, bound the search to the supported entity-length window before looking for ';'; give XML decoding a monotonic parser or bounded entity grammar. Remove PartFs's redundant relationship decoding when upstream supplies normalized attributes; retain the linear XML-helper repair for its other callers and the separate bounded HTML-helper repair. Preserve canonical literal '&' part names and one-time entity normalization through round trips. Preserve the standalone XML helper's documented permissive output for unsupported or unterminated references while making its work linear. Apply practical relationship-target length/work bounds as defense in depth, preserving exactly one normalization pass and the standalone helper's linear permissive behavior. Align admission/DOM attribute token boundaries or reject unsupported unquoted syntax as defense in depth. Preserve the linear XML decoder fix for this comment-to-attribute route; removing only the redundant relationship decode does not cover it. Apply the bounded HTML helper consistently to Markdown raw-HTML block text and attribute consumers, using UTF-8-safe bounded lookahead and preserving recognized entities, malformed literal retention and multibyte text.

findings.title: Python and Node plan recording can overwrite unrelated files through staging symlinks
findings.summary:
The Python and Node CLIs write plans through a predictable .<plan>.<PID>.partial pathname using nonexclusive truncating writes. A local actor who can create entries in the plan directory can preplace a symlink there and make the victim overwrite another file it can write, before the intended plan replacement.
 Assigned discovery-0032 corroborates both non-dry-run recorders after successful plan preview. Intentional final-plan symlink resolution is distinct from the independently substituted staging entry.
findings.remediation:
Use exclusive, unpredictable staging owned by a private directory, hold the opened handle through writing, and rename that verified file. Reuse the native publication design or equivalent mkstemp/exclusive wx APIs and never follow existing staging entries. Python can reuse native publication; Node needs equivalent secure publication semantics. Preserve intentional final-plan symlink resolution to its authorized resolved target while securing the separate staging object; successful recording installs a verified regular plan file and failure preserves prior output.
Additional retained remediation detail: Use an exclusively created private staging directory/file held by handle, verify staged bytes, and atomically publish to the authorized plan target. Refuse preexisting staging objects and preserve intended final-plan symlink semantics without following a staging symlink.
